nozzles: Mounted deck gun smooth bore tip
sceneElements.elevation: Mounted deck gun; no elevation add-on for deck-gun height

problems.title: Deck Gun Flow
problems.question: Engine 181 is operating a deck gun with a 1¾-inch smooth bore tip at 80 PSI nozzle pressure. Use GPM = 29.7 × diameter² × √NP. What is the approximate total deck gun flow?
problems.instructorExplanation: A 1¾-inch smooth bore master-stream tip at 80 PSI flows about 815 GPM.
problems.explainMistake: This is a flow question, not a pump-pressure question.

problems.title: Pump Discharge Pressure
problems.question: Engine 181 is operating a deck gun mounted directly on the apparatus with an 80 PSI smooth-bore nozzle-pressure requirement. This training problem assigns no discharge-hose loss, appliance loss, or elevation add-on. What pump discharge pressure should be set?
formulaBreakdown: PDP = NP + FL + elevation + appliance loss.
problems.instructorExplanation: With no additional losses assigned in this scenario, pump discharge pressure equals nozzle pressure.
problems.explainMistake: Do not add an elevation value merely because the deck gun sits above the pump panel.

problems.title: Alternate Deck Gun Tip Flow
problems.question: Engine 181 switches to a 1½-inch smooth bore deck gun tip at 80 PSI nozzle pressure. Use GPM = 29.7 × diameter² × √NP. What is the approximate flow?
problems.instructorExplanation: A 1½-inch smooth bore tip at 80 PSI flows about 600 GPM.
problems.explainMistake: Use the changed tip diameter in the flow formula.

problems.title: Scenario Pressure-Drop Chart
problems.question: Engine 181 is supplying one 815 GPM deck-gun stream. Hydrant static pressure is 80 PSI and residual pressure is 65 PSI. For this chart-reading exercise only, use: pressure-drop % = (static - residual) ÷ static × 100; 0-10% = 3 additional equivalent streams, 10-15% = 2, 15-25% = 1, over 25% = 0. According to the stated chart, how many additional equivalent 815 GPM streams are indicated?
formulaBreakdown: The scenario chart maps 15-25% to 1 additional equivalent stream.
problems.instructorExplanation: This question tests use of the chart supplied in the prompt. It is not an NFPA 291 available-flow calculation.
problems.explainMistake: Use only the chart stated in this question; do not present it as a universal hydrant-capacity rule.

problems.title: Additional Attack Line Flow
problems.question: The deck gun is flowing 815 GPM. If one additional 185 GPM attack line is placed in service, what is the new total flow requirement?
problems.instructorExplanation: Add both flowing devices for total water demand.
problems.explainMistake: This is a total-flow question, not a pump-pressure question.
